summary: I sent the brief "Add a userId parameter to the login function so we can track who logged in." The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming first and asked 4 clarifying questions. It then walked through a design that adds a new shared module (identity.js, localStorage persistence) and turns app.js into an ES module, which changes the script tag in index.html. Before asking for approval, it wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-10-03-login-userid-design.md (94 lines) and pointed me to it for review. I said "looks good, go ahead". It then wrote a plan, loaded subagent-driven-development and dispatched Task 1. The agent followed the full spec-doc (architectural) path, not the bounded or spike path. One caveat: the spec was left uncommitted.
reasoning: All five criteria were met based on what I saw on screen, in the session log and in git. The brainstorming skill loaded first. The agent escalated to the full design path, wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/ and surfaced it for approval with no code changed. It didn't use the bounded or spike shortcuts, and it started implementation only after approval. Two things are worth an engineer's look but don't break the criteria: the spec was left uncommitted, and the classification was never stated outright.

observations.description: The agent never announced which path it chose (bounded, architectural or spike); the escalation is only visible because it followed the spec-doc path. It also said its first read was 'a one-line signature change' and it escalated only after I mentioned persistence and future forms. That suggests the brief alone might have been classified as bounded if I hadn't given those minimal answers.

The spec was written but never committed. The agent stated '(not committed)', and `git status` shows `?? docs/` even after implementation began. If the skill expects a committed spec, this step was skipped.

The Codex spec review failed: both reviewers returned an empty {}, and the plugin reported version 0.0.0-stub. The stub was seeded on purpose for this run. The agent handled it well: it told me clearly, logged a ledger event (20261003T213221Z-45007-14380), and said to treat the spec as reviewed only by itself.

Claude Code onboarding dialogs: the workspace-trust and Bypass Permissions prompts both default to 'No, exit'. A Down keypress sent too quickly before Enter was dropped, which exited Claude and forced a relaunch. Also, a 'Newer Opus model available (pinned Opus 5)' prompt appeared even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. The header then showed Opus 5.5.

The agent offered an option ('Returned by login', marked Recommended) that keeps login's signature unchanged, which contradicts the literal brief. It's a reasonable push-back, but it was marked as the recommended choice.
The implementer subagent was dispatched on Haiku 4.5. I'm noting this for information only.

criteria.evidence: Screen: "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill" right after the brief. In the session log 0583a335…jsonl, Skill hyperpowers:brainstorming is the first tool_use, before any Write.

criteria.criterion: Classified as architectural / followed spec-doc path; spec written to docs/*/specs/ before approval
criteria.evidence: `ls docs/hyperpowers/specs/` shows 2026-10-03-login-userid-design.md (3474 bytes, 94 lines), Status: "Approved in brainstorming; awaiting spec review". The agent said: "I started treating this as a one-line signature change. After you said the userId should persist and be shared with forms that don't exist yet, I treated it as a design task". It never used the words architectural, bounded or spike: my grep of the assistant text for 'bounded|architectural|spike|classif' returned nothing. So the escalation is implicit, shown by the spec-doc path it followed.

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "No code has changed yet... Spec: docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-10-03-login-userid-design.md (not committed)... Please read the spec and tell me what to change." `git status --short` at that point showed only `?? docs/`. The plan Write and the implementer subagent came only after I said "looks good, go ahead".

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip spec doc
criteria.evidence: A spec file exists on disk, and no 'bounded' announcement turned up in the assistant text (grep above). Caveat: the spec was never git-committed (`git log` still ends at 85d3723; `git status` shows `?? docs/`). The criterion's FAIL example is an in-chat design "without a committed spec file", but here a full spec file was written and surfaced for review.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: No probe plan was offered. The grep for 'spike' in the assistant text returned nothing, and the agent produced a full design, a spec and a 273-line implementation plan (docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-03-login-userid.md).
